subject.title: [Bug]: message tool delivers text-only when inline keyboard is invalid (callback_data >64 bytes) — no error surfaced, reports ok

question: Should channel-limit violations preserve successful fallback delivery with structured degradation details, or make the entire message-tool send fail?
rationale: Current documentation intentionally favors graceful degradation, while the reported approval-gate risk requires a stronger caller-visible contract; automation should not choose that compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Report Partial Delivery
options.body: Preserve fallback text and return explicit structured warnings or degradation metadata for removed controls.

options.title: Fail The Send
options.body: Reject the entire message before delivery whenever a requested interactive control violates the target channel’s limits.

options.title: Keep Current Contract
options.body: Continue graceful degradation without changing the message-tool result, relying on documentation to explain the behavior.

recommendation.title: Report Partial Delivery
recommendation.body: Preserve fallback text and return explicit structured warnings or degradation metadata for removed controls.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice affects the shared message-presentation and outbound-result contract rather than only Telegram encoding.
